hero_intro: Welcome to the Brubru EFPIA Brief. The freshest EU pharma and health moves from the last 48 hours, with what Brubru is tracking for you underneath. Every item links straight to the answer inside Brubru: a chat you can interrogate, your calendar, or the file's own page. A quiet end to the week on the regulatory wires, so this is a focused read: health security, the next health committee sitting, the Biotech Act evidence base, and antimicrobial resistance.

headlines.title: EU health security group met this week, reports just published
headlines.source: DG SANTE Latest Updates, 27 and 28 May 2026
headlines.snippet: The Commission has published the reports from the General Working Group of the Health Security Committee, which met on 27 May, alongside the summary of an ad hoc working group on 26 May. This is the layer that coordinates Member State and Commission action on serious cross-border health threats: preparedness, surveillance and joint procurement. EFPIA's vaccines and antimicrobial members read it for the earliest signals on the next joint-procurement and stockpiling waves.
headlines.ask: What did the EU Health Security Committee working group discuss this week, and how does EU joint procurement of medicines work?

headlines.title: Parliament's health committee sits Wednesday 3 June, agenda published
headlines.source: European Parliament SANT subcommittee, draft agenda for 3 June 2026 (published 28 May)
headlines.snippet: The Parliament's public health subcommittee has published the draft agenda for its next sitting on Wednesday 3 June, built around the EU health workforce, health resilience and disease prevention. This is the room where the pharmaceutical package and the Critical Medicines Act follow-up move. If you have a file in front of this committee, this is the moment to confirm your shadow engagement. Open your EU calendar to see it alongside the institutional dates that week.
headlines.ask: What is the European Parliament public health committee likely to discuss at its 3 June 2026 meeting?

headlines.title: The Commission published the evidence base behind the Biotech Act
headlines.snippet: The Commission published the analysis underpinning the Biotech Act proposals, the Regulation and the companion work on genetically modified microorganisms. The document sets out the rationale, the pillars and the governance design. The proposal is still on the table at the European Parliament: no rapporteur has been appointed and no lead committee designated yet, so treat any named MEP or vote date with caution. Read the Brubru deep dive for what is known versus what is not.
headlines.ask: What does the Biotech Act analysis cover, and what is its status in the European Parliament?

headlines.title: The EU's AMR One Health Network has published its latest meeting papers
headlines.source: DG SANTE Latest Updates, published 28 May 2026
headlines.snippet: DG SANTE has published the presentations from the latest meetings of the AMR One Health Network, the expert group that coordinates Member State action on antimicrobial resistance across human health, animal health and the environment. Antimicrobial resistance sits at the intersection of three EFPIA priorities: the pharmaceutical package incentives debate, the Critical Medicines Act, and health-security coordination. Ask Brubru how the EU's One Health approach and the incentive mechanisms fit together.
headlines.ask: What is the EU's One Health approach to antimicrobial resistance, and what does the AMR One Health Network do?
